general.title: S. Korea Inflation Stays Sticky, Backing BOK’s Tightening Bias
general.summary: South Korea’s pace of inflation stayed firm in September, signaling persistent price pressures and supporting the case for the central bank to keep its tightening bias.

general.title: Software roared back last quarter. Cramer says these stocks can keep climbing
general.summary: Software stocks bounced back from their AI-driven sell-off, while chip stocks cooled after a massive first-half run.

general.title: Cocktail of Risks Boosts Demand for Safest Bonds: Markets Wrap
general.summary: Risks spanning credit markets, elevated commodity prices and French political turmoil boosted demand for safer government bonds, snapping a prolonged decline fueled by persistent inflation concerns.

general.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Oct. 2
general.summary: Oil steadied after a two-day gain as the US sent an additional aircraft carrier to the Middle East, potentially escalating the war with Iran and threatening to hamper a recovery in energy flows.

general.title: Russell Reynolds CEO on C-Suite Leadership & New Book
general.summary: Constantine Alexandrakis, who leads Russell Reynolds Associates and wrote The Catalyst CEO, joins to discuss the leadership challenge and the idea that CEOs cannot drive transformation alone. The discussion broadens into a larger question about what kind of CEO is needed when a company requires both cultural repair and strategic disruption. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: Nike Earnings Disappoint as China Sales Lag
general.summary: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are Ferguson CEO Kevin Murphy, Envestnet CEO Chris Todd, Nuveen CEO Bill Huffman, EY Global Vice Chair Andrea Guerzoni, Allspring Global Investments Head of Equity Investments Ann Miletti, Mastercard Economics Institute Chief Economist Michelle Meyer, CFRA Equity Analyst Zachary Warring, Sports Marketing Consultant Joe

general.title: EY-Parthenon’s Guerzoni on Latest CEO Outlook Survey
general.summary: In an exclusive interview on Bloomberg The Close, Andrea Guerzoni, EY Global Vice Chair, discusses a pullback in EY Parthenon’s latest CEO outlook survey. Guerzoni points to the survey’s confidence reading falling from a record 62% to 51% and asks why that drop occurred, noting it is a decline but not a collapse. He speaks to Romaine Bostick & Emily Graffeo on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: Accenture stock rallies after earnings beat expectations
general.summary: Shares of Accenture surged Thursday after the company's fiscal fourth-quarter results beat estimates.

general.title: Nike shares drop as retailer posts disappointing sales, announces layoffs as part of restructuring
general.summary: Nike is expected to post another quarter of declining sales as the company tries to turn around its business and regain growth in China.

general.title: Breaking Down Nike's 'Disappointing' Earnings
general.summary: CFRA Equity Analyst Zachary Warring discusses Nike’s latest quarterly results and strategic shift. Speaking on "Bloomberg The Close," Warring says that despite maintaining a buy rating, he calls the quarter and full-year guidance disappointing, noting double-digit revenue declines and earnings per share below his expectations. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: Ferguson CEO on the State of the AI Buildout in the U.S.
general.summary: Kevin Murphy, CEO of Ferguson, joins the program to discuss broader manufacturing conditions. Murphy notes that manufacturing appeared to emerge from a multiyear slump earlier in the year, helped by several tailwinds, and asks whether that momentum is still holding as the final three months of the year begin. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Emily Graffeo on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: Why ‘Manchesterism’ May Face an Uphill Battle
general.summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham wants to roll back decades of neoliberalism. Bloomberg Originals shows the hard choices coming amid a grim fiscal landscape.

general.title: Rising Yields Are Wreaking Havoc on Stocks Outside the AI Trade
general.summary: After the 10-year Treasury yield rose as high as 5.34% for the first time since 2002, stock traders are fiercely debating when the selloff in bonds will start to trigger pain for a resilient US stock market.

general.title: Anthropic Said to Plan Pre-IPO Investor Day as Listing Nears
general.summary: Anthropic PBC is set to meet prospective investors on Oct. 14 in preparation for its initial public offering, according to people familiar with the matter, advancing its plan for a potential blockbuster listing even amid scrutiny over AI safety.

general.title: United Airlines gets aggressive in battle for top Delta, American flyers
general.summary: United Airlines launched an aggressive status match program for Delta and American's top frequent flyer elites.

general.title: US Further Targets Iran-Linked Russian A7 Financial Network
general.summary: The US imposed a new round of sanctions on Russia’s A7, a financial services firm accused of using a global network of shell companies to move funds for sanctioned businesses, including in Iran.

general.title: Amazon Jet Lacked Wind Data Before Miami Crash, NTSB Says
general.summary: An air traffic controller didn’t provide an Amazon.com Inc. cargo plane with wind information prior to it crashing at Miami International Airport last month, killing five people on the ground, according to accident investigators.

general.title: Bank of Canada Won’t Target House Prices With Interest Rates
general.summary: The Bank of Canada’s second in command said the central bank is limited in what it can do to address home prices, arguing that the housing market should remain an input and not a target of interest rate decisions.

general.title: Jefferson Says Fed May Need More Time to Weigh Next Move
general.summary: Two Federal Reserve officials, including Vice Chair Philip Jefferson, suggested policymakers should take more time before deciding whether additional interest-rate increases are needed to slow inflation.
